prompt: CHALLENGE: Target: p-bromoaniline (BrC₆H₄NH₂) from benzene. Which sequence works?

options.label: Nitrate (gives nitrobenzene) → reduce to aniline → protect NH₂ as acetanilide (Ac₂O) → brominate (acetamide is o/p director, gives para) → hydrolyze acetamide back to NH₂.
Brominate first (gives bromobenzene) → nitrate (NO₂ is meta director — gives meta, not para) → reduce — wrong isomer.
Nitrate → brominate (NO₂ is meta director; gives m-bromonitrobenzene) → reduce — wrong isomer.
Treat benzene with HBr and NaNH₂ simultaneously.

explanation: Free NH₂ oxidizes under Br₂/FeBr₃ conditions and over-brominates. Protect as the acetamide (-NHCOCH₃) first — still o/p directing (through resonance), but tames reactivity. One Br goes para. Hydrolyze back to NH₂. Classic 5-step aromatic synthesis.
